author: Melanie Tucker
title: Much needed relief: New Providence opens cooling station - NewsBreak
text: As outdoor temperatures/humidity reached into the unbearable range in Blount County on Tuesday and Wednesday, a group of volunteers was ready with iced-down bottles of water, cooling towels and hospitality. New Providence Presbyterian Church, centrally located on West Broadway in downtown Maryville, opened a cooling station inside where anyone trying to escape the oppressive heat could do just that. Hours were 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Tuesday and 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Wednesday. Volunteers Ellie Morrow and Ted Higgs took the first shift on Wednesday. Early in the day residents of Maryville Towers stopped by for water and cooling towels. Chairs were lined up were they could sit for as long as they liked. Louden Young, associate pastor of emerging generations and mission, is one of the leaders at New Providence who helped get this station operational. He said there had been talk a few years ago about creating such a resource, much like the warming center operates out of First Baptist Maryville when temperatures dip into the 20s. It was now time to put a plan into action for summer’s dangerous heat. “We had two days where the heat index was going to be over 100 degrees,” Young said, referring to Tuesday and Wednesday. He said he discussed the idea of a cooling station with Raeann Reihl at United Way and then other members of New Providence staff. “We all green-lighted it right away,” he said. Emails went out and United Way of Blount County came on board to help with getting the word out and also securing water donations. United Way had a few fans they were offering to give out earlier in the week. On Tuesdays, New Providence opens its doors for a free meal, from 5-6 p.m., so some who came for the cooling station also stayed for the meal. “This kind of felt like an extension of that,” Young said. The whole project from idea to implementation happened quickly. Young said his church will look at the possibility of opening the cooling station more days in August. “This is hopefully moving toward a more permanent solution where next summer we could open something similar to the warming center.” He said he welcomes suggestions on how to serve better. Going forward, hours might get moved up to later in the day, he added. Dena Rackliff, a 54-year old resident of Maryville, has been displaced out of one apartment and flooded twice at another. She said only one room of her apartment is livable. She said she appreciates the kindness of New Providence. She arrived on Wednesday morning to cool off. “I’ve been walking since November,” she said, having to park her truck due to mechanical issues. Floyd Hodges was another one who came to cool off. He said he’s currently living on the streets. He was told about the cooling station from staff at the Blount County Public Library and walked over to New Providence before noon on Wednesday. He said he knew there were others on their way. “We didn’t expect a whole lot of participation this first time because it’s new,” Young explained. “You have to get established so people know you are here.” No questions are asked of those who stop by, other than what else they might need. Morrow and Higgs said their church can build up the program as needs are made known. Momentum is growing, Young added. “With so much going on in our world and so many place where we are deciding what we can’t do for our neighbors, it’s time we start having more conversations about what we can do,” Young said.
